title: Running Agents in Parallel
one_liner: Claude Code offers five ways to run several tasks at once. Choose by who coordinates the work, whether workers communicate, and whether they edit the same files.

core.title: Five approaches, one kind of worker
core.body: **Subagents** (delegated workers inside one session), **agent view** (dispatch and monitor background sessions), **agent teams** (a lead with coordinated teammates), **dynamic workflows** (a script that runs many subagents) and **projects** (long-running cloud threads). In every case the workers are Claude sessions.
core.why: They differ in control and location, not in capability. Pick by how involved you want to stay.

quotes.text: Claude Code has five ways to work on several tasks at once
quotes.label: Run agents in parallel

quotes.text: In every approach the workers are Claude sessions.
quotes.label: Run agents in parallel

core.title: Choose by three questions
core.body: Who coordinates: Claude inside one conversation (subagents), you (agent view), a lead Claude (agent teams), or a script (workflows). Do workers need to talk to each other? Do they edit the same files?
core.why: Answering these three questions removes most of the ambiguity between the approaches.

quotes.text: The right approach depends on who coordinates the work, whether the workers need to communicate, and whether they edit the same files
quotes.label: Run agents in parallel > Choose an approach

core.title: Results flow back differently
core.body: Subagents report to the conversation that spawned them. Agent view sessions report only to you. Agent team teammates message each other directly. Sessions you run yourself can share findings through cross-session messaging.
core.why: Pick an approach that delivers results where you need them.

quotes.text: Subagents report results back to the conversation that spawned them, and agent view sessions report results only to you.
quotes.label: Run agents in parallel > Choose an approach

core.title: Isolate file edits with worktrees
core.body: When parallel work touches the same files, give each session or subagent its own git worktree. Agent teams do not use worktrees, so split the files between teammates.

quotes.text: Agent teams don't isolate teammates in worktrees
quotes.label: Run agents in parallel > Choose an approach

core.title: Parallel work multiplies cost
core.body: Each running session or subagent consumes tokens. Running many at once raises usage proportionally.
core.why: Parallelism trades tokens for wall-clock time.

quotes.text: Running several sessions or subagents at once multiplies token usage.
quotes.label: Run agents in parallel

practice.title: Map your next task to an approach
steps: Pick a real task, such as a refactor across 20 files
Answer: who coordinates, do workers communicate, do they share files
Name the approach and whether worktrees are needed
practice.check: You can justify the choice with the three answers.
practice.variation: Change one answer (for example, workers now share files) and see which approach changes.

practice.title: Find each status command
practice.goal: Learn where to check on running work.
steps: Start a background subagent in a session
Run `/agents` and note that it only points to subagent file locations
practice.check: You can say which command shows background items in the current session.
practice.variation: Run `claude agents` from your shell and compare.

gotchas: `/agents` (in a session) and `claude agents` (agent view) are different commands.
Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default.
`/batch` is a packaged use of subagents and worktrees, not a separate coordination style.

cheatsheet.meaning: Open agent view for background sessions.
List, attach to or stop background items in this session.
List workflow runs and their phases.
Split one large change into 5 to 30 worktree-isolated subagents.
